speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when this rash first appeared and whether it started on your trunk before spreading to your limbs? Also, are you currently taking any new medications or supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her face look like "slapped cheeks," and are the spots on her body flat and red with a lacy pattern? Have you noticed if the rash becomes more visible after she takes a warm bath or spends time in the sun?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "slapped cheek" appearance and lacy body rash strongly suggest Erythema Infectiosum, but I need to confirm one last detail before finalizing my diagnosis. Does she have any history of anemia or immune system disorders that might complicate this viral infection?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: With the classic "slapped cheek" appearance, lacy rash, and lack of complicating medical history, the clinical picture is confirmed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).
